$comment: Places where a cited DEV/ADR id has no entry, with a reason AND a kind.
kind: 'deliberate-mention' — the id is named IN ORDER to say it is missing,
or the file is a verbatim archive whose text must not be rewritten. These
kind: 'deferred-fix' — the citation IS wrong and reads as a real
cross-reference, but fixing it is blocked on something outside this file.
These require a `tracked` task id and are printed on every run so they
cannot quietly become permanent. An allowlist that cannot tell these apart
converts real errors into permitted ones, which is the failure mode the
verifier identified when this file was introduced.
Scoped by file, not file:line, so the allowlist survives edits above a
citation. The cost is a whole-file blast radius: a NEW wrong citation of the
same id in an allowlisted file is suppressed silently. Keep the list short.

allow.reason: The verifier's remit uses DEV.38 as the worked example of why the dangling check exists — a citation that propagated from a prompt into three documents, and that meant two different things in different places.

An archive of the Stage B prompts exactly as they were pasted into Claude Code. The prompt did say DEV.38; editing it would rewrite the record of what was asked, which is the only thing this file is for.
Same — a verbatim prompt archive. DEV.41 was the prompt's name for a premise that never became an entry; the decision that was actually taken is recorded as DEV.43.

Same — verbatim prompt archive. Described in the prompt as 'correlated subquery ambiguity'. No entry exists and none of the citing context says what was decided, so it cannot be resolved: unresolvable, not guessed.

Every site names DEV.38 in the course of recording, or quoting text that records, that the id has no entry — which is why naming it is the point and correcting it is not possible. Enumerated rather than counted: DEVIATIONS.md:4767 ("DEV.38, DEV.41 and DEV.42 were cited as real in 13, 4 and 1 places respectively"), :4771 and :4773 (a quoted operator instruction, and the finding, in DEV.128 — "three cited DEV ids had no entries"), :4835 (a quoted acceptance criterion naming the deferred-fix entry for DEV.38 in PROJECT_PLAN.md) and :4845 (a table row reading "from F.63's own notes, which name DEV.38 to say it is missing"), and :4963 and :4965 inside DEV.130, which names it while recording that the citation was corrected during the F.63 migration. Line numbers are the reading taken when this was written and they drift as the file grows; the stable form is "every mention inside DEV.128, DEV.129 and DEV.130".

Appears inside DEV.43's 'Spec said' field, quoting the original chunk prompt verbatim. The quotation is accurate — the prompt really did cite DEV.41 — and DEVIATIONS.md is append-only, so historic entries are not edited.
DEV.128 records that DEV.42 was cited without an entry and what it turned out to mean. Naming the missing id is the content of that record — the entry exists to say the id does not.
F.72's notes record which ids were dangling and what each turned out to mean. Naming them is the content of the record.
Same — F.72's notes.
Same — F.72's notes. DEV.42 is recorded there as unresolvable.
Same — records that a prompt's mis-citation propagated into three documents, which is the argument for this check existing.
Prose that exists to explain that DEV.38 has no entry. Naming the missing id is the content.
The comments now describe the cross-tenant bug in place and state that no DEV.38 entry exists. The id is named only to say it is dangling.

PROJECT_PLAN.md is generated in its entirety from docs/stage-f-tasks.json (F.37/F.63), so every DEV.38 here is rendered from a task note that names the id in order to say it does not resolve — F.63 and F.72 both do exactly that, and DEV.128 is the entry recording which id was meant. CONVERTED from kind: deferred-fix, not deleted: the wrong citation this entry was tracking lived in the hand-maintained Stage B B.10 row, which moved to docs/PROJECT_HISTORY.md and was corrected there during the migration. Deleting the entry instead would have made the surviving generated mentions newly dangling — five occurrences across the two table rows for F.63 and F.72.

The path checker's docblock quotes the incident that demonstrates mutual coverage: its own allowlist reason once read "Mirrors the DEV.38 entry for check-id-references.mjs", and check:ids rejected it because DEV.38 deliberately has no entry. The id has to be named for the anecdote to make its point — a version with the id elided would not show what was rejected. Mirrors the existing entry covering the id checker's own docstring, which names DEV.38 for the same reason.
